subject: Plan streamlining & rollback decision tree
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emily Torres <emily@wellpath.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Plan streamlining & rollback decision tree

Emily —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. I pulled together a short set of options to simplify WellPath's current pilot packaging so procurement can evaluate faster. Attached is a lightweight decision tree we'd like to use to map your desired outcomes to a default plan. High level:

- Option A (Consolidated): single Tier with seat pool + feature flags. Lowest operational risk, small up-front commitment.
- Option B (Modular): 2-tier with add-on feature bundles. Better price granularity, more admin for your team.
- Option C (Burst-first): metered throughput with seat overlay — ideal if usage is spiky.

For each path I included rollback guardrails (timing windows, prorations, and a short rollback-matrix). My ask: please tell me which outcome you want prioritized — cost predictability, lowest initial spend, or flexible burst capacity — and we’ll pin the fallback path and discount level.

Attachments: plan-streamline-draft.pdf (decision tree), rollback-matrix.xlsx

If procurement needs a single-number summary for the SOW, we can produce a one-page summary by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0194

From: Emily Torres <emily@wellpath.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, WellPath Procurement <procurement@wellpath.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Plan streamlining & rollback decision tree

Jordan —

Appreciate the quick turn. A couple notes from procurement that will affect which option we choose:

- We need a hard rollback window of at least 30 days tied to usage reconciliation.
- Any multi-tier discount must include a clear stepdown penalty if we drop below thresholds.
- We prefer a proposal that calls out data residency and audit log retention for the pilot (already flagged by security).

Can you provide a one-line summary for each option (annual cost, expected overage cadence) and explicitly call out where the 30-day rollback sits? If you can get that to me by Monday afternoon, procurement will move to an internal review.

Also cc'd procurement@ for visibility.

Best,
Emily Torres
Head of Product Operations
WellPath, Inc.

On Fri, May 14, 2027 at 09:12 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:

> Thanks again for the time yesterday...

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Plan streamlining & rollback decision tree — internal options

Team —

Quick internal recommendation after reviewing Jordan's draft and WellPath's asks:

1) Default: Offer Option A (Consolidated) as the standard commercial path with a 30-day rollback window and prorated credits for usage-based refunds. Rationale: procurement wants predictability; consolidated limits admin overhead.

2) Alternate: Option B (Modular) as a priced add-on if they insist on feature-level controls — include a 10% migration credit if they move from B -> A within the first 6 months.

3) Discounting: For pilot -> enterprise conversion, propose a staged discount: 15% for annual commit, 8% for 6-month commit. Do not exceed 20% without RevOps sign-off.

4) Security/data: call out VPC option as an add-on and include default audit log retention (90 days) in the pilot SOW.

I attached a simple rollback-matrix that maps time windows to credit calculations (see rollback-matrix.xlsx). Ben — can you confirm the migration credit math? Priyom — any runtime constraints we should call out if we pick 'Consolidated' (e.g., seat pooling + dedicated capacity)? Lauren — verify that CS can support a 30-day rollback operationally.

-Kim

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Plan streamlining & rollback decision tree — technical notes

Kim / team —

Short technical clarifications to include in the proposal:

- If we default to Option A (Consolidated) but they request an initial seat pool + burst overlay, we should define the burst SLA separately (e.g., 5x burst for 2 hours/day best-effort) and not include it in the rollback calculus. Rollback should cover baseline committed capacity only.
- Migration credit is fine; ensure that the KV cache migration and model variant pinning are documented — switching from a modular variant to the consolidated variant can take up to 48 hours for a full cache warmup on dedicated pools.
- For data residency: include a clause that pilot logs are retained for 90 days; enterprise can extend retention with a paid add-on.

I can add a short technical appendix to the proposal that calls out those timings.

—Priyom

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emily Torres <emily@wellpath.ai>, WellPath Procurement <procurement@wellpath.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 14:00:00 -0700
Subject: Updated proposal: consolidated pilot + 30-day rollback (attached)

Emily / procurement team —

Per our notes, attached is an updated, single-page proposal and SOW summary that reflects:

- Path chosen: Option A (Consolidated) — single Tier with seat pool, optional burst overlay.
- Rollback: 30-day rollback window from activation date; credits prorated to unused committed capacity per the attached rollback-matrix.xlsx.
- Discount: 15% for an annual pilot commit, 8% for a 6-month commit. Migration credit (10%) if they move to a modular plan within 6 months.
- Security: pilot includes 90-day audit log retention; VPC/on-prem options quoted as an add-on.
- Next steps: sign SOW (DocuSign link in email), legal review (we’ll add the residency clause), kickoff scheduled within 7 business days of signature.

Attachments: WellPath_PROPOSAL_v2.pdf, rollback-matrix.xlsx

If this looks good, please reply with a confirmation and procurement contact and we'll send a DocuSign.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Emily Torres <emily@wellpath.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: WellPath Procurement <procurement@wellpath.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Updated proposal: consolidated pilot + 30-day rollback (attached)

Jordan / team —

Thanks — procurement reviewed and we're prepared to proceed with the consolidated pilot and 15% annual discount. A couple of small redlines from legal: add explicit language that the 30-day rollback applies to committed baseline capacity only (per Priyom's note) and call out the audit log retention period in the SOW.

Procurement contact: Mark Delgado (mark.delgado@wellpath.ai) — he'll take the DocuSign and route for signature.

Please send the DocuSign with those two clarifications and we'll aim to return signed within 3 business days.

Appreciate the responsiveness — Emily

---
